question: In August 2025, the Indian Army, together with IIT Madras, set up a research centre on the IIT Madras campus called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agnishodh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Indian Army** formalized a significant collaboration with the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras** to boost domestic technological capabilities.
 
• The partnership led to the establishment of a specialized research centre named **Agnishodh**, located directly on the **IIT Madras campus** in **Chennai**.
 
• **Agnishodh** is designed to serve as a hub for **advanced research** and **innovation**, specifically tailored to meet the evolving needs of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• The core mission of the centre is to achieve **indigenization** of critical technologies, focusing on sectors like **battlefield electronics**, **secure communication**, and **automated systems**.
 
• By leveraging the intellectual resources of **IIT Madras**, the **Indian Army** aims to create **indigenous solutions** that reduce the **defence sector's** dependence on **foreign imports**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat in Defence**: 
 
 
• The establishment of **Agnishodh** is a strategic move under the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) initiative.
 
• The **Ministry of Defence** has set a target to achieve a turnover of **USD 25 billion** in **defence manufacturing** by **2025**.
 
 
 
• **Role of IIT Madras**:
 
 
• **IIT Madras** has a long-standing reputation for **defence R&D** and already hosts the **DRDO-Industry-Academia Ramanujan Centre of Excellence**.
 
• The institution provides a fertile ground for **startups** and **incubation cells** to work on **dual-use technologies** that benefit both **civilians** and the **military**.
 
 
 
• **Technological Focus Areas**:
 
 
• **Agnishodh** will prioritize the development of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** for **predictive maintenance** of military hardware.
 
• Other focus areas include **Quantum Computing** for **cryptography** and the development of **Swarm Drone** technologies for **surveillance**.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Strategy**:
 
 
• The centre facilitates direct interaction between **Army personnel** and **researchers**, ensuring that the **prototypes** developed are **operationally viable** in harsh environments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Modernization of the Army**: The **Indian Army** is undergoing a massive **modernization drive** to prepare for **non-contact warfare** and **cyber-electronic** threats.
 
• **Strategic Location**: Placing **Agnishodh** in **Chennai** allows the **Indian Army** to tap into the **industrial corridor** of **Tamil Nadu**, which is one of India's two **Defence Industrial Corridors** (the other being in **Uttar Pradesh**).
 
• **Budgetary Support**: Funding for such initiatives is often supported by the **iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence)** framework, which aims to provide **financial grants** to **innovators** and **SMEs**.
 
• **Collaboration Scope**: While **IIT Madras** provides the **academic expertise**, the **Indian Army** provides **domain knowledge** and **field testing** facilities, creating a **synergetic ecosystem** for **defence innovation**.
